National Assembly
Twenty-first Session
Complete Minutes
Proceedings
23
Ashad 2083
Wednesday
Meeting Number - 26
The National Assembly's meeting today commenced at 12:27 PM under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson, Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the proceedings of today's National Assembly meeting (12:27 PM) begin. Honourable members, names have been received to speak during the Zero Hour. A time limit of one minute each has been set for speaking during the Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Gita Devkota.
Honourable Member Gita Devkota (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, I extend heartfelt condolences and deep sympathy to the bereaved families on the tragic incident that occurred in Bharatpur Metropolitan City-23 on the night of Ashad 20th, where a wild elephant named Dhurthe killed a mother and son while they were sleeping at home. Chairperson, it is said that Dhurthe the elephant has already killed about 24 people, but the government still seems busy with meetings, reports, and relief announcements. If citizens are not safe even while sleeping at home, where is the state's security? Conservation of wildlife is necessary, but not at the cost of human life. Dhurthe should be immediately controlled and kept in a secure enclosure or under special surveillance. The affected families should be provided with adequate relief and justice. Effective fencing, surveillance, and safe relocation of high-risk families in settlements around Nikunj should be done immediately. The government must now provide security, not just condolences. Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan.
Honourable Member Dharmendra Paswan (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, I wanted to say something about the government's 100 days regarding security. Instead of stopping incidents in the Madhesh, incidents have increased. Among various reasons, the accused are roaming freely. The victim Maju Sada from Suri Municipality Ward No. 3, who was supposed to be safe in a safe house in Krishnasabarn Rural Municipality, is still safe, but the main accused is roaming freely and has not been caught. Through the Chairperson, I strongly urge the government to immediately apprehend and take action. 
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur.
Honourable Member Mahanta Thakur (Loktantrik Samajwadi Party, Nepal):- Honourable Chairperson, due to the destruction of the Chure-Bhawar region, water sources in the Madhesh have dried up, fields have dried up, and paddy transplantation has not occurred. There is a shortage of drinking water. Even hand pumps have dried up, and nothing has been done by the government so far. Thank you, Jai Madhesh.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhala.
Honourable Member Meenasingh Rakhala (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Chairperson, how long will Karnali suffer? Why do we only hear news of accidents, disasters, and state neglect every day? A passenger Force vehicle going from Surkhet to Kalikot fell into the Karnali River, and the vehicle has not been found yet. The exact number of passengers is unknown. The victim families are worried. In Jumla's Hima Rural Municipality, one person died and two were injured due to lightning strikes, and many sheep died. Similarly, in a road accident in Dolpa, one person lost their life, and others are undergoing treatment. I offer heartfelt condolences to the departed souls and express deep sympathy to the bereaved families. I wish the injured a speedy recovery. I have a clear demand from the government: adequate compensation for the families of the deceased, free and effective treatment for the injured, and that roads, rescue, and disaster management in Karnali be given high priority. Karnali's citizens should not be treated as second-class citizens. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri.
Honourable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, I want to draw the government's attention to the news I have been seeing in recent days. This government came with the slogan of good governance. It is reported that many people in the hierarchical bureaucracy have resigned, and dozens of advisors have been appointed at the level of first and second-class officers, receiving salaries and facilities equivalent to ministers. What is this? People who chanted the slogan of good governance will not run the administration through a hierarchical bureaucracy, and is this the way for the unelected to rule Singh Durbar? I request that the concerned ministers or the Prime Minister's Office provide information to the House regarding this, and I want to inform the public. Through the Honourable Chairperson, I request information in writing as to which decision granted them this authority, and how can they do this beyond their commitments? (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha.
Honourable Member Rekha Kumari Jha (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, today I want to draw the government's attention to some important issues directly related to the daily lives of the people: education, housing, health, and good governance. First, I want to talk about the education sector. Before coming to power, the government had pledged to control the arbitrary fees of private schools, reduce the financial burden on parents, and systematize the education sector, but today the opposite is seen. Many private schools have not fully complied with the regulations set by the government. They are collecting money under other headings. Thank you, Regards.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Roshi Mechhe.
Honourable Member Roshi Mechhe (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, on one hand, policy documents claim the country is free from load shedding, and on the other hand, the government is boasting about exporting energy to neighboring markets. If our own citizens are kept in darkness, is our energy policy focused on fulfilling national needs or merely on propaganda for foreign trade? The Terai is burning with 40-degree heat, industries are shut down, and low voltage is burning refrigerators and fans in people's homes. This is not a shortage of electricity, but the extreme managerial helplessness of the Nepal Electricity Authority. What is the use of increased production when the distribution system reaching the consumer's doorstep is four decades old and dilapidated? Therefore, I want to draw the attention of the Ministry of Energy, Water Resources, and Irrigation to initiate urgent structural reforms by establishing an emergency fund for the technical upgrading of last-mile distribution infrastructure. Citizens who pay the state their dues have a legal right to uninterrupted energy, which is consumer sovereignty. The fees paid by the public are for light, not for the state's... (Time expired.)
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire.
Honourable Member Basudev Ghimire (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, I condemn the atrocities, the manhandling, and the violence that the government perpetrated against the visually impaired who were protesting for their rights at Maitighar. Through the Honourable Chairperson, I want to ask the Home Minister of the Government of Nepal: is this an excellent example of the good governance this government talks about, or an excellent example of violence? Thank you, Jai Nepal.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota.
Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, it seems the Council of Ministers amended the Education Act on Ashad 18th. It has been stipulated that individuals with political party membership cannot serve as members and chairpersons of the School Management Committee. A provision has been made that only individuals who have not been affiliated with any political party for at least 4 years prior to the formation of the School Management Committee can be members, which curtails people's political rights. Political rights are among the most important aspects of human rights; they are also fundamental rights. In a class society, there are class ideologies; a person without ideology cannot be conceived. It is the government's foolishness to treat politics like a criminal offense and restrict entry into the education sector. This decision by the Council of Ministers seems similar to the transfer of mayors; attention should be paid to this. Regards, Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Member Somnath Poudel.
Honourable Member Somnath Poudel (Nepal Communist Party, UML):- Honourable Chairperson, news is circulating in the media that the landless squatters kept at the holding centers in Nagarkot and Bode have been brought to various places like Koteshwor and left stranded on the streets. The government, which claimed to provide a long-term solution, bulldozed the shanties of these landless squatters without even providing prior notice, and after two and a half months of bulldozing, they have been brought and left on the streets. I strongly condemn and denounce this act. The Prime Minister and ministers of the government are not listening to the cries of the landless and poor citizens. I believe there is a problem with their hearing capacity. If they cannot hear such cries, there must be some problem with their ears. Therefore, I demand that a specialist doctor be arranged to treat the ears of the Prime Minister and the ministers. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable members, the Zero Hour speaking session concludes here. Honourable members, the Ministry-wise Question and Answer session will now commence. Honourable members, after the Honourable Minister responds, if the questioner Honourable member wishes, they can ask a supplementary question related to their question within 1 minute. Now, Honourable members, I invite the Honourable Minister of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Sunil Lamsal, to the rostrum to answer the questions posed by the Honourable member.
Honourable members, now I provide time to the questioner Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma to ask his question.
Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepali Congress):- Honourable Chairperson, through the Honourable Chairperson, I want to ask the Honourable Minister. Regarding the Khulalu-Hilsa section of the Karnali Corridor, specifically the Khulalu-Sallisalla and Simikot-Hilsa sections, many concrete bridges have been left incomplete since their inspection, and most have not even started construction or are incomplete. What is the actual progress status of these bridges? What are the main obstacles in their construction? What steps has the government taken to expedite the work through contract processes and resource management, and by when is the entire project targeted for completion? I request clarification. Thank you.
Right Honourable Chairperson:- Honourable Minister.
Honourable Minister of Physical Infrastructure and Transport, Mr. Sunil Lamsal:- Honourable Chairperson and Honourable members, specifically regarding this road, there are currently about 8 bridges mentioned in the details. I have not visited the site yet, but there is a program to visit the site, and this road section is also a high priority for us. Currently, a total of 9 bridges are to be advanced through the Design and Build method and 2 through contract packages, and details have been received. However, based on our site study, we will build all the bridges that need to be built.

Currently, the monitoring of all under-construction projects will also be rigorous. Rather than reading out the details of such objective matters here, I will go and see them in the field. I will go to the field and see what problems exist. After resolving all the problems, I reached there on the 3rd of Shrawan, and I have resolved all the issues you raised through an on-site inspection. Since the government's agenda for this year is to manage the budget and advance the procurement process for all the bridges in that section, I will provide you with further details after returning from there, or I will provide them here in the assembly. Thank you. - Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, as the questioning honorable member wishes to ask a supplementary question, I provide time to ask a supplementary question focused on the subject. Honorable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, through the Honorable Chairperson, I wish to ask a supplementary question to the Honorable Minister. The Karnali Corridor is not only the backbone of Karnali Province but also of the neighboring provinces in terms of trade and development. It is a tragedy that the design of five concrete bridges has not yet been approved after such a long time, and landslides in many places have not been controlled. Due to the narrow road, hundreds of Karnali residents lose their lives annually. We need to manage sufficient budget to expand and upgrade the Karnali Corridor to a two-lane road, complete it within the stipulated time by achieving 100% capital expenditure, promote tourism, and open the Hilsa-China border to improve the economic condition and living standards of the country as well as the people of Karnali. What projects and plans have been formulated for this? (...Time expired.) Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. Honorable Minister of Physical Infrastructure Development, Mr. Sunil Lamshal: - Honorable Chairperson, regarding the issues of Karnali and the road that you have raised, the government has set a goal to complete all single-lane roads into double-lane roads within three years, similar to the structures you mentioned, as the highest priority. There is sufficient budget for it, and we will start the work by preparing DPRs and estimates in this fiscal year. The road section you mentioned, along with roads connecting all district headquarters and all local level headquarters, will be tendered this year. All of them. For all the municipalities in Mugu district or Karnali Province where road access is not yet available, or where the road is unpaved or unsafe, we have allocated sufficient budget this year to make them double-lane, and all district headquarters double-lane. Due to excessive accidents and many deaths occurring there, we have advanced this program to end such incidents permanently. Regarding landslides, we have also managed a special budget and will complete all identified landslides within the next three years, and we will immediately tender all studies conducted this year and conduct studies for those remaining and then tender them. We have also prepared DPRs for that. We will definitely solve the problem you mentioned in this section, and we are also working on the other border. Since this is also part of our tourist road, we will advance this work with special priority, and I believe we will build roads up to the China border. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Now I request the Honorable Minister to take his seat. Honorable members, I request the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, to come to the rostrum to answer the question posed by the honorable member. Honorable members, now I provide time to the questioning honorable member Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" to ask her question. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, first of all, I would like to thank the Honorable Minister through the Honorable Chairperson. She is present in this meeting of the National Assembly to fulfill her responsibilities and answer questions. My question is as follows: According to the price analysis report 2083 published by the Department of Commerce, Supply and Consumer Protection, there have been excessive fluctuations in the prices of food items. Nepal Oil Corporation has increased the price of petroleum products six times in the months of Chaitra and Baishakh alone. The increase in fuel prices has made transportation fares more expensive, directly impacting the prices of food and consumer goods, while the increase in aviation fuel prices has led to an increase in domestic airfares. This has not only burdened the poor people but has also pushed the overall economy towards inflation. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, Greetings. I express my gratitude for the interest shown in the work of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, and for the suggestions and queries raised. Thank you for providing me with time to present the answer in the esteemed house. I wish to present the answer to the question raised by Honorable Member Madan Kumari Shah Garima. The Department of Commerce, Supply and Consumer Protection, along with five commercial offices under the department, including the Kalimati Fruits and Vegetable Market Development Committee, Nepal Food Kirana Business Association, Nepal Retailers Association, Nepal Oil Corporation, and the Department of Nepal Rastra Bank, have collected data through field inspections and various sources. Based on the analysis of this data, the monthly price analysis report is being published. In this context, according to the price analysis report for the month of Baishakh 2082/083, published on the department's website, fluctuations have mainly occurred in the prices of local ghee, beans, cowpeas, bottle gourd, green beans, cucumber, and other vegetables. The report concludes that the unnatural fluctuation in vegetable and fruit prices from farmer to consumer within a month is influenced by the increase in petroleum prices, the state of vegetable production, and intermediaries at various market levels. Nepal Oil Corporation regularly adjusts the prices of petroleum products through an automated system. Despite the recent unfavorable situation in the Middle East, facilitation is being provided in the management of petroleum product supply. Along with this, to maintain market price transparency, control unnatural price increases, prevent artificial shortages, and protect consumer interests, the department conducts daily field inspections of importers, producers, and sellers. If any irregularities are found, fines are imposed immediately in accordance with the Consumer Protection Act, 2075, and the inspection report is made public daily through the department's website. It is also informed that after the date this answer was sent, Nepal Oil Corporation has significantly reduced the prices of petroleum products, as honorable members are aware. Subsequently, airfare and transportation fare rates have also been adjusted. The ministry wishes to urge representatives of private sector organizations to adjust the prices of other goods. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable members, now the questioning honorable member... Honorable Minister, please wait a moment. As the honorable member wishes to ask a supplementary question, I provide time to ask a supplementary question focused on the subject. Honorable Mr. Madan Kumari Shah "Garima" (Nepal Communist Party): - Honorable Chairperson, thank you for the answer. You have admitted that intermediaries have an influence on price increases. What measures has the government adopted to prevent this? Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: - Honorable Minister. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - We have activated the Commerce Department, and they are working through three channels daily. They are conducting inspections everywhere and making efforts to control prices. They are working every day. Honorable Chairperson: - Now I request the Honorable Minister to take his seat. Honorable members, I would like to inform you that the discussion on the appropriation titles of the Appropriation Bill, 2083, received with a message from the House of Representatives, will be followed by answers from the concerned Honorable Ministers. Accordingly, the schedule has been set for the concerned ministers to answer the questions raised during the discussion on the appropriation titles related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, Ministry of Physical Infrastructure Development, Ministry of Home Affairs, Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation, Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Defense, Office of the President, Office of the Vice President, Office of the Prime Minister and Council of Ministers, and the Secretariat of the National Planning Commission. Honorable members, if clarification is required regarding the answers of the concerned ministers regarding the appropriation titles, only the honorable members who participated in the discussion on the appropriation titles of the concerned ministry will be able to seek clarification. Honorable members, now I provide time to the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari, to answer the questions raised during the discussion on the appropriation titles related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Ms. Gauri Kumari: - Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, Greetings. I express my heartfelt gratitude for providing me with time in the esteemed house to answer the questions raised by the honorable members regarding the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies during the discussion on the annual budget for the fiscal year 2083/084. The important statements, suggestions, and guidance expressed by the honorable members during the discussion on the annual budget for the fiscal year 2083/084 have provided encouragement to the ministry to make its future performance effective and to facilitate the industrial and commercial environment. I would like to express my gratitude to the honorable members for their positive suggestions regarding the allocated budget and programs for the ministry and its subordinate bodies. The collective guidance of the honorable members has also inspired the implementation of the budget and programs through inter-ministerial coordination. The government has presented the budget for the upcoming fiscal year as a base year with the goal of achieving 7% annual economic growth, building an economy of 100 billion dollars in 5 years, creating more than 1.2 million jobs, and increasing domestic production and productivity. I wish to inform you that the budget and programs for this year have been presented with investment efficiency, utilizing available resources to achieve the goals set by the government. Honorable members...

Development, promotion, investment promotion of industry and business, concessions and facilities for domestic industries, collateral-free loans for youth with skills and readiness to bear risk, business development services, improvement of service delivery using digital technology, and other arrangements to increase domestic production and create employment, the government is sincerely committed to this. In this context, I would like to shed light before the esteemed House on the upcoming budget for 2083/084 and the questions raised by the honorable members during the discussion on the budget and programs. A total of 17 honorable members presented their views during the budget discussion. All honorable members expressed their views focusing on production, employment, trade, entrepreneurship, supply management, revival of sick industries, and other related issues. It has been expressed by the honorable members that there is a need to create a conducive production, investment, and business environment by coordinating and interconnecting various ministries of the Government of Nepal. I would like to pledge that the ministry will remain active in increasing production, productivity, and employment by further enhancing inter-ministerial and inter-level coordination and boosting the morale of the private sector. For this, the ministry is in the process of preparing investment protection and promotion and policy formulation to be approved by the Council of Ministers of the Government of Nepal. This strategy aims to establish private property protection, investment protection, and industrial estates as peaceful sectors. The strategy also provides for various concessions and facilities to revive industries that have been closed and sick due to the damage caused during past movements. Under the Startup Entrepreneurship Loan Program targeting youth who wish to start businesses, I would like to inform you that loans are being processed for 966 projects in this fiscal year through collateral-free loans at subsidized interest rates. I would like to assure you that this program will be implemented more effectively in the coming fiscal year as well, and the ministry is also preparing an action plan for budget implementation to bring the allocated budget into implementation from the beginning of the fiscal year. Honorable Chairperson, some new programs have also been included in the upcoming fiscal year's program. Among these, a budget of 34 crore has been allocated for the National Enterprises Facilitator Program. Through its implementation, the process of formulating procedures to make policy facilitation, program implementation, inter-agency and inter-level coordination, startup business activity services, and business promotion services more effective for micro, small, and medium enterprises and startups is underway. Under the employment-linked production sector program, new industries will be established in the previously announced industrial areas with the objective of creating more employment by providing plots. The ministry has already started the process of managing and operating the industrial estates located in various places for the industrialization of the country. In this context, I would like to inform you that the Industrial Area Management Limited has started the process of collecting approximately 43 crore 46 lakh in outstanding land lease payments and providing land to actual productive industries to increase production and employment. Honorable Chairperson, I am now going to respond sequentially to the questions raised by the honorable members regarding the budget and programs of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce, and Supplies. The suggestions and questions raised by the honorable members include: branding Nepali products and making them quality, facilitating tea exports, diversifying exports and markets, purchasing paddy for the year, developing export strategies for tea, cardamom, etc., increasing budget for startup loans, formulating policies to create employment, establishing organic fertilizer industries, promoting SMEs, reducing production costs, production of packaged organic jaggery, marketing, implementing coffee promotion programs, producing raw materials for the garment industry, operating rural industries, reducing trade deficit, renewing the TIFA agreement, ensuring smooth supply of petroleum products and establishing an automatic pricing system, lack of value addition in processed exports, formulating policies for economic prosperity, industries in Biratnagar and other places not running well, unemployment and lack of production due to closures, operating the Hetauda Garment Industry, operating existing industries rather than talking about them, lack of budget for petroleum exploration, export-oriented industries, green industries, promoting PPP models, etc. Honorable Chairperson, I would like to express my commitment that the government is taking the issues raised by the honorable members seriously and implementing them with priority, and these issues will be further addressed through the budget and programs of the next fiscal year. A task force has been formed to find a long-term solution to the problems seen in tea exports from Nepal to India, and its report is being prepared. Diplomatic efforts have also removed the existing obstacles, and a smooth export system is now in place. To address the storage problem of tea and cardamom and expand market access, resources have also been managed for the storage and warehouse construction of tea and cardamom with cost-sharing from the entrepreneurs of the concerned sector. The purchase and distribution system for paddy and wheat at the minimum support price is being carried out through the Food Management and Trading Company Limited, and this has been prioritized in the budget for the upcoming fiscal year. Honorable Chairperson, the ministry has prioritized the development of commodity-specific export strategies and export promotion for goods with export potential identified in the Nepal Trade Integration Strategy 2080. In this context, draft export strategies for three commodities, namely ginger, chupi, and carpets, have been prepared. In the upcoming fiscal year, export strategies for other commodities mentioned by the honorable members will also be prepared and implemented sequentially. In line with the government's policy to promote startups, the Startup Fast Track Action Plan, which includes a 100-point agenda, has been approved and implemented, and a Startup Fast Track Help Desk has also been established at the Industrial Business Development Foundation. Furthermore, a significant amount of resources has been allocated within the available limit for the upcoming fiscal year to provide concessional loans to startup enterprises. Various programs for promoting entrepreneurship and skill development to create employment and self-employment opportunities within the country have been included in the budget for the upcoming year. Through programs such as socially inclusive entrepreneurship, women's entrepreneurship, business development centers, national entrepreneurship services, and youth entrepreneurship, encouragement, skills, and technology will be provided to those wishing to start businesses, I would like to inform the honorable members through the esteemed Chairperson. Honorable Chairperson, some honorable members raised the issue of lack of programs to reduce costs and promote SMEs, and the branding of organic products. In this regard, the Industrial and Trade Logistics Master Plan, prepared with the objective of reducing industrial and trade logistics costs and facilitating trade, has been approved and will be implemented with promptness. I also wish to inform you that the preparation of the National Productivity Master Plan is underway to increase productivity in the industrial sector. Furthermore, through the annual budget, to enhance the competitive capacity of productive industries, the electricity demand charge has been reviewed and a concession in electricity tariff has been provided, and its implementation is underway. The ministry is also making efforts for a special electricity tariff for small and medium-sized industries. Programs for packaging, marketing, and export promotion of Nepali organic products are being operated through the Trade and Export Promotion Center, and various programs have been proposed for the upcoming fiscal year. Regarding rural industries, the Government of Nepal has initiated the process of evaluating the assets and liabilities of seven government-owned industries. Based on this study, the modality of industry operation will be determined. I would like to inform you that industries in Biratnagar and other closed and sick industries across the country will be managed through a transparent process. A study report has been prepared for the revival of the Hetauda Garment Industry, and cleaning, maintenance, and trial production are underway through the Directorate of Military Material Production. We are trying to operate it as a means to replace imports, develop self-reliance, create employment, and increase the contribution of the industrial sector to the economy. Honorable Chairperson, the government has formulated and is implementing an action plan with priority to reduce the trade deficit, and we have requested the US government to extend the period of Duty-Free, Quota-Free facility under the Nepal-US Trade Agreement, which has expired. Despite the difficult situation created in West Asia, the supply management of petroleum products in Nepal has been effective. To protect consumer interests, daily market monitoring has been intensified by the Department of Commerce, Supply, and Consumer Protection in coordination with various agencies. During this period, a Price Transparency Week was also organized, the information of which I would like to share with this House. An Investment Express policy has been adopted to promote domestic investment and attract foreign investment. For this, a system for approving foreign investment entirely online has been adopted. This will reduce the time and cost for investors. All types of services are being gradually transformed into virtual mode through the One-Stop Service Center. Preliminary studies have confirmed a natural gas reserve of 112.1 billion cubic meters in the Jaljale area of Dailekh, and based on its utilization, there is a theoretical basis for producing 200 MW of electricity daily and 2200 tons of urea fertilizer and vehicle fuel. The major challenges for this project include the development of basic infrastructure such as roads, electricity, and drinking water required for commercial excavation and the management of large-scale investment. In this context, I would like to inform you that the process of prioritizing the establishment of a subsidiary company of Nepal Oil Corporation to determine the investment modality, formulate sector-specific national standards, and collaborate with universities for technical manpower development is underway. The plan is to proceed with the project in a phased and systematic manner by intensifying detailed technical and economic feasibility studies, and resources will be managed accordingly. To start the project, and to convert to electric boilers and furnaces, cleaner production, green

and to promote EV charging at petrol pumps. I request that this be noted. Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to express my commitment to seriously consider and effectively implement the valuable suggestions and concerns raised by the Honorable Members after in-depth study of the budget and programs of the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies and its subordinate bodies. Thank you. (13:08 hrs) Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, I will provide time to Honorable Members who wish to seek clarification regarding the response given by the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari. I have allocated 1 minute for each Honorable Member seeking clarification. Honorable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota. Honorable Shri Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, through you, I did not see a proper response to the points I raised with the Minister of Industry. I had raised the issue of cannabis. Why was it not included that cannabis should be legalized, brought within the legal framework, and taken as an industry? And another thing, coffee can be internationalized, not just national. No information came about coffee either, for which I seek a response. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Goma Devi Timalsina. (13:10 hrs) Honorable Shri Goma Devi Timalsina (Communist Party of Nepal): Honorable Chairperson, today our Industry Minister has brought very good things with great effort. Despite that, I feel that some things are incomplete. Now, the Hetauda Industrial Estate was inspected. According to the inspection, it has been said that cleaning has been done. When will this industry start operating? And how much budget has been allocated for it? That also needs to be known, needs to be stated. How many public enterprises are there across the country? How many are closed? How many are operational? How many are waiting to be revived? How many need to be closed? (... Time expired.) 97 Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Ram Kumari Jhankri. (13:11 hrs) Honorable Shri Ram Kumari Jhankri (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honorable Chairperson, through you, I would like to ask the Honorable Minister two or three questions. Specifically, the Hetauda Textile Industry. I heard about its operation in the priorities and principles of the policy program and budget. What is the modality of its operation? Similarly, the Gorkhakali Rubber Industry was also a subject that came up in the priorities and principles of the policy program and budget. What has happened regarding its operation and what is its modality? Similarly, there was talk of operating the Dhaubadi Iron Industry, I saw it somewhere in the policy program. What is happening with it? On the other hand, since there are many ministries in this budget, I couldn't see much. However, regarding reducing the trade deficit and creating a self-reliant economy, the contribution from Industry and Commerce is not much, while Commerce's contribution is significant. Regarding these issues, there are many questions, but what is happening with these issues? I seek information. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Now, to provide clarification regarding the clarification sought by the Honorable Member, I will provide time to the Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Gauri Kumari. Honorable Minister of Industry, Commerce and Supplies, Shri Gauri Kumari: Thank you. Yes. The responsibility of creating a local environment for products like coffee has been given to the local government under the micro-enterprise development program. All that is being done through the DDI, which is currently with the Ministry of Finance. Based on the report that comes through the DDI, we have decided to operate other rural industries. I have written to the Ministry of Finance for the release of 3.3 million rupees for the textile industry, which has already been released. It has gone to the Hetauda industry, and the repair work has also started. I want to assure you that it will come into operation in a few months. Thank you. 1t Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Members, the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Industry, Commerce and Supplies concludes here. Honorable Members, now I will provide time to the Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Gita Chaudhary, to answer the questions raised in the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment. Honorable Minister of Agriculture, Forests and Environment, Shri Gita Chaudhary: Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the Honorable Members for participating in the discussion on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment under the Appropriation Bill, 2083, and for providing valuable suggestions and raising queries. Honorable Chairperson, regarding the budget allocation for the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment for the fiscal year 2083/084, the Honorable Members have primarily raised queries and suggestions regarding the overall budget allocation for the ministry being low, the budget only covering large farmers, the status of chemical fertilizers, the budget allocated for fertilizer management, human-wildlife conflict management, damage to crops, regulation and management of subsidies, agricultural bills, facilitation of tea cultivation exports, climate change, watershed conservation, river system management, etc. The Honorable Members have suggested increasing the budget for the agricultural sector, ensuring easy availability of production materials such as fertilizers, seeds, and irrigation, expanding the access and scope of agricultural insurance, allocating adequate budget for agricultural research programs, the National Agricultural Modernization Program, subsidies for organic fertilizers, small-scale irrigation and similar programs, promoting organic and biological fertilizers, providing relief to farmers, effective implementation of minimum support prices, and facilitating the promotion and export of tea and coffee cultivation. I express my sincere gratitude for these valuable suggestions and seek permission to present my views on the queries raised by you. 99 Honorable Chairperson, Honorable Members, I would like to inform you that a total of 73 billion 120 million has been allocated for the ministry. For the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, the major programs under the ministry include 32 billion 460 million for chemical fertilizer supply, which is approximately 59 percent of the agricultural budget. I would like to inform you that 2 billion 190 million has been allocated for agricultural insurance, 1 billion 500 million for incentive grants to sugarcane farmers, 340 million for subsidies for organic fertilizers, 2 billion 640 million for agricultural research programs, 2 billion 620 million for the National Agricultural Modernization Program, and 1 billion 530 million for the Hill Fruits and Vegetables Development Project, 1 billion 450 million for the High-Value Agricultural Commodities Development Project, 970 million for the National Chure Conservation Project, 1 billion for the Climate Resilient Chure Program, and 880 million for the Biodiversity and Watershed Management Program. Similarly, budget allocations have been made with special priority for human-wildlife conflict management and sustainable forest management programs. Honorable Members, a large portion of the overall budget in agriculture is spent on the import of chemical fertilizers, and this amount increases every year. It is clear that sustainable development in the agricultural sector is not possible unless we seriously focus on alternatives. Accordingly, the ministry is moving forward with necessary plans and programs. I would like to share my views on the issue of low budget allocation in the agricultural sector, the budget targeting large farmers, and the management of the agricultural subsidy distribution system. I would like to inform the Honorable Members that the ministry's budget and programs have been proposed within the allocated budget ceiling. The overall budget for the ministry appears to be somewhat lower due to the pressure on national resources. As the Honorable Members have pointed out, I share the same understanding that the budget allocation in the agricultural sector is not sufficient. However, I request that efforts have been made to formulate effective budgets and programs according to the available budget ceiling. Regarding the budget allocation in the agricultural sector, I would like to inform you that efforts and initiatives necessary for the development of the agricultural sector are being undertaken through the integrated efforts of the federal government, provincial governments, and local levels, due to the limited scope and structure of the Federal Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock Development. Honorable Members, regarding point no. 24 (a) of the budget statement for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, there seems to be some confusion among the Honorable Members regarding the pilot program where the government will provide up to 40 percent incentive grants to farmers for initial capital investment of up to 20 million rupees for agricultural and livestock production. I would like to inform you that this program is a pilot program of the current government, and efforts are underway to prepare a modality for its implementation in which both small and large farmers can participate, and the ministry is actively working to develop an appropriate modality for small farmers to invest by joining groups and for large investors to invest individually. Furthermore, continuity has been given to programs and projects that have been in operation to provide agricultural facilities and concessions to small, medium, and large farmers, and necessary budgets have been allocated. The ministry is making necessary efforts to make agricultural subsidy distribution transparent and effective. I would like to inform you that a task force has been formed to analyze and study the subsidies provided in the agricultural sector over the past 10 years, and necessary work is underway. I would like to inform you that more than 75 percent of the budget allocated for the agricultural sector under the ministry is directly beneficial to small farmers. Every year, fertilizer is provided to approximately 2.2 million farmers through more than 14,000 agricultural cooperatives, more than 150,000 agricultural insurance policies are issued, incentive grants are paid to the accounts of more than 60,000 sugarcane farmers, artificial insemination services are extended to more than 700,000 livestock, approximately 60 million doses of vaccines are provided, and through programs such as expanding the cultivation area of various crops, expanding the irrigated area through small-scale irrigation, and promoting mechanization, small, medium, and large farmers directly benefit. Due to limited resources, the budget for agricultural research programs and agricultural modernization has been proposed to be somewhat lower, but programs and activities have been proposed in a way that achieves the expected goals by prioritizing programs and activities. In the upcoming fiscal year, under the National Agricultural Modernization Program, necessary budgets have been allocated for activities targeting production and productivity enhancement, modernization, and commercialization in specific production areas through 21 super zones and 206 zones, and for the operation of 239 new pocket areas for various crops.

Regarding chemical fertilizer, seeds, irrigation availability, and budget and programs: For the supply of chemical fertilizer in the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, an amount of 32 billion 460 million has been allocated. The action plan for the supply and management of fertilizer for the upcoming fiscal year has already been prepared. In the current fiscal year 2082/083, an amount of Rs. 28 billion 820 million was allocated for the supply of chemical fertilizer, and as of Ashad 19, 2083, 458,000 metric tons of fertilizer have been imported. Including the previous year's stock, 412,000 metric tons of fertilizer have been sold and distributed. Currently, there are 95,000 metric tons in stock, and an additional 50,000 metric tons are expected to be supplied soon through G2G. Thus, the required fertilizer for the paddy season appears to be readily available. I would like to inform the honorable members that a commitment has been received from the Ministry of Finance to provide additional budget if necessary to ensure there is no shortage of budget for fertilizer supply. I also inform you that the action plan for the supply and management of fertilizer for the upcoming fiscal year has been prepared. To address complaints regarding the distribution and availability of chemical fertilizer, contact persons have been arranged at the Ministry of Agriculture, Provincial Ministries. Regarding the availability of seeds, improved seeds and quality seeds developed by farms under the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the Department of Agriculture have been made available to producers, seed producer groups, cooperatives, farmers, and private companies. The private sector has been made more responsible for seed production and management. To promote indigenous and local seeds, a budget and program have been arranged to provide subsidies for quality seeds to farmers in 153 local levels through digital technology.
Regarding the expansion of irrigation facilities: The Ministry allocates budget for the construction and maintenance of small-scale irrigation structures through national projects and conditional grants. For conditional grants, approximately 160 million rupees have been allocated for the construction and expansion of small irrigation structures in 156 local levels. For national projects, an allocation of 47 million rupees has been made for the construction and expansion of small irrigation structures. Through the Ministry of Energy, Irrigation, and Water Resources, large-scale irrigation projects are underway, which are expected to provide easy irrigation facilities to arable land in the Madhesh, Lumbini, and Sudurpashchim provinces in the coming days. Coordination is being maintained with the Ministry of Energy, Irrigation, and Water Resources for the expansion of the irrigation sector.
Honorable members, regarding tea quality and international trade access for Nepali tea: To expand tea cultivation commercially, budget has been allocated to provide technical support for tea cultivation to small farmers by identifying potential new districts and areas such as the hilly regions of Gandaki and Bagmati provinces. The Ministry has initiated the process of amending the National Tea and Coffee Development Board Act, 2049, and the National Tea Policy, 2057. An agreement has been signed between the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the National Tea and Coffee Development Board, prioritizing research work for the development of new tea varieties, soil testing, and pest and disease management. To facilitate tea exports smoothly, the Government of Nepal and the Ministry have taken necessary technical and diplomatic initiatives to resolve the problems of tea exporters, and the issue of tea export has now been resolved. To further establish the national trademark of Nepali Orthodox tea, 'Nepal Tea Quality from the Himalayas,' in the international market, the Board is conducting promotional programs in coordination with Nepali embassies abroad. The Ministry has prioritized necessary coordination with the Ministry of Industry to enact laws for the geographical indication (GI) and intellectual property protection of tea. While orthodox tea produced in Nepal is gaining international recognition, cooperation has begun with the private sector to develop a national symbol for CTC tea that reflects its distinct identity and quality. Furthermore, the Ministry has prioritized the participation of tea entrepreneurs in international fairs through the joint efforts of the National Tea and Coffee Development Board and the private sector for the promotion of Nepali tea brands. To address non-tariff barriers faced during Nepali tea exports, particularly in India and other countries, necessary work is being carried out through the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control to align Nepali National Tea Standards with Indian FSSAI and International Codex Standards. The Ministry is coordinating necessary work through the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control, the Department of Weights and Measures, and the Trade and Export Promotion Center to facilitate tea exports, and further information on this matter is expected to be provided to the assembly by the relevant ministry.
Regarding the coffee cultivation promotion program: In the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, an amount of 19.2 million rupees has been allocated for programs such as coffee seedling production, coffee cultivation expansion, and training on coffee farming for lead farmers through the Coffee Development Center, Aamchaur, Gulmi. Additionally, budget has been allocated for the operation of a coffee demonstration plot and a model coffee garden of 10 ropanis in potential coffee-producing districts of the mid-hill region under the National Tea and Coffee Development Board.
Regarding providing farmers with weather forecast information: To mitigate potential losses in the agriculture sector due to weather and disaster-related causes, an early warning system has been arranged through the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology. Similarly, preliminary information dissemination activities to minimize damage from weather and disasters are being carried out by the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the Agricultural Information and Training Center.
Regarding subsidies for organic fertilizer and promotion of organic farming: To discourage the increasing use of chemical fertilizers and promote organic farming, a budget of 350 million rupees has been proposed for organic fertilizer subsidies at the federal level and 112.4 million rupees as conditional grants at the provincial level. Furthermore, necessary budget has been proposed for soil health improvement programs in 250 local levels, green manure promotion programs in 39 local levels, and organic farming promotion programs in 35 local levels. Similarly, under the National Forest Development and Management Program, budget has been allocated for the operation of programs related to organic fertilizer production and management of invasive species in each province through federal conditional grants. Arrangements have been made to provide incentives and subsidies to excellent farmers who produce compost fertilizer by utilizing leaf litter from forest areas, and to conduct composting and organic fertilizer production and testing programs using wildlife biological materials.
Regarding agricultural insurance and mitigation of disaster-related damages and relief: In the upcoming fiscal year, a target of issuing approximately 150,000 agricultural insurance policies has been set, and a budget of Rs. 2 billion 190 million has been proposed for agriculture and livestock insurance. To make the agricultural insurance program accessible and effective, as per new policy provisions, an amount of Rs. 1 billion has been sent as provincial conditional grants to be implemented by provincial ministries from the upcoming fiscal year. To mitigate losses in the agriculture sector due to weather and disaster-related causes, an early warning system has been arranged through the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology, and preparations are underway to implement it more effectively in the upcoming fiscal year. Similarly, necessary programs and budget have been arranged for the dissemination of preliminary information regarding potential damages from weather and disasters by the Nepal Agricultural Research Council and the Agricultural Information and Training Center. Details of birds that died due to bird flu have been collected, and relief has been provided to the concerned farmers. For this, 500 million rupees have been reallocated in the current fiscal year, and the necessary budget has been allocated for the upcoming fiscal year. Coordination is being maintained with the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and the provinces to provide relief to farmers through a one-door system by collecting details of damages in the agriculture sector due to disasters.
Regarding the issue raised by honorable members about monkeys and other wild animals destroying crops and the need for control programs: This is a very important issue and a matter of special concern for the Ministry. For the long-term solution to the problems caused by monkeys, the Government of Nepal has formed a study committee with the participation of relevant bodies and scientists. Based on the recommendations of the report submitted by this committee, programs for monkey management, human-wildlife conflict mitigation, and farmer welfare will be implemented sequentially. Arrangements have been made to manage the necessary budget and programs for capacity building and pilot programs in cooperation with local and provincial levels for monkey control. I would like to inform you that in the coming days, the Ministry will continue to implement necessary policies and programs with the objective of strengthening farmer security, protecting agricultural production, and promoting human-wildlife coexistence.
Regarding watershed management, river system management, and disaster preparedness to mitigate risks: Under the National Chure Conservation Program, activities such as gully and landslide control, embankment construction, river and stream bank protection, river management using bio-engineering techniques, wetland conservation and management have been carried out in the Chure and Terai-Madhesh regions, with an allocation of Rs. 970 million. Similarly, an amount of Rs. 240 million has been allocated for activities related to the development of Koshi, Gandaki, Karnali, and Mahakali rivers, river and stream bank protection, water source conservation, multipurpose use of water sources, and watershed management.
Regarding the human-wildlife coexistence program: Under the human-wildlife coexistence program, arrangements have been made for expenditure on directly result-oriented programs such as pond construction, solar fence construction, grassland development, purchase of wildlife handling and rescue equipment, construction of mesh wire fencing for the protection of arable land, and construction of other infrastructure for human-wildlife conflict mitigation. In response to the concerns expressed by honorable members, budget has been allocated for training and workshops as it is legally necessary to conduct capacity development, livelihood conservation awareness, and skill development training programs for the community in accordance with the Intermediate Area Management Regulations, 2052. I request that the budget be allocated for training and workshops.
Regarding declining production, increasing imports, and the promotion of production and commercialization in the agriculture sector: To increase production and productivity in the agriculture sector, the budget for the upcoming fiscal year has allocated the necessary budget for the implementation of programs targeting major crops, livestock, and fisheries. Although agricultural imports have increased due to changes in the eating habits and lifestyles of general consumers, increasing demand, imports of raw soybean, palm, and sunflower oil for export purposes, and the customs policies of neighboring countries, the domestic production of agricultural products such as fresh vegetables, eggs, meat, and milk remains satisfactory. Under this program, arrangements have been made to produce compost fertilizer by collecting leaf litter from forest areas for forest fire control, provide grants as incentives to outstanding farmers, produce compost and organic fertilizer using forest-based biological materials, and conduct testing programs. This is expected to contribute to forest area cleanliness, forest fire reduction, soil fertility conservation, and the development of a sustainable agricultural system by gradually reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers. In that context, there was concern about the purchase of DAP fertilizer at a higher price, regarding which I have already informed you that the government has supplied 5 lakh 58 thousand 9 hundred metric tons of fertilizer so far in the current fiscal year and distributed 4 lakh 42 thousand 4 hundred metric tons to farmers. I have also informed you that local administrations have been activated to take legal action against cooperatives or dealers involved in misappropriation and malpractice in subsidized fertilizer distribution, and grievance officers have been arranged at the federal ministry and focal persons at the provincial ministries to hear complaints related to fertilizer. In recent years, the demand for chemical fertilizer in the country has been increasing extremely, and the use of farmyard manure, compost, and green manure in the soil has been decreasing significantly, leading to an excessive increase in dependence on chemical fertilizers. Since chemical fertilizers are not produced domestically, dependence on the international market directly affects fertilizer prices and supply. We are all aware of the impact of the wars in Israel, Iran, and America on fertilizer production, supply, and prices. The government has been providing large-scale subsidies to farmers for chemical fertilizers. Currently, the cost of 1 kg of urea is Rs. 85 and DAP is Rs. 167. Farmers receive 82 percent and 74 percent subsidy, respectively, for both these fertilizers. When international market prices fluctuate, the cost and subsidy percentage also fluctuate. A month ago, urea reached Rs. 160, and as the demand and price of fertilizer increase excessively, the government's financial burden and fiscal pressure both increase. Furthermore, the excessive use of urea and less use of phosphorus and potassium-based fertilizers lead to a decline in soil health and quality due to the imbalanced use of chemical fertilizers. The ministry is serious about this, and budget has been arranged for the upcoming fiscal year to operate programs in collaboration with all three tiers of government to improve soil health and promote organic farming. I would like to earnestly request all honorable members to take special initiative in educating and raising awareness among the general public about the balanced use of chemical fertilizers and saving the soil. Honorable Chairperson, I would now like to seek permission to clarify the issue related to chemical fertilizer raised by the honorable Narayan Dutt Mishra. The Government of Nepal has designated the Agricultural Inputs Company Limited and the Salt Trading Corporation Limited to purchase and distribute chemical fertilizers to farmers on subsidy. These fertilizer distribution companies prepare cost estimates and accept bids that are substantially effective in terms of minimum price according to the procedures and processes stipulated by the Public Procurement Act, 2063, and the Public Procurement Regulations, 2064. The cost estimate for every fertilizer purchase contract is done at the rate. A question was also raised regarding whether the government purchased DAP fertilizer at a high price. For the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of DAP fertilizer, a bid was invited on February 27, and on March 12, 2083, the estimated cost per kg was USD 1.10488, but a bid was accepted at USD 1.101, which is 0.35 percent less than the estimate. Similarly, for the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of DAP fertilizer through G2G, a contract was signed on June 1, 2026, at USD 1.10218 per metric ton, which is 1.40 percent less than the estimated cost of Rs. 1117.81. Therefore, since the fertilizer was purchased based on international market prices, the issue of being expensive or cheap is not relevant. Regarding the question that India purchased the same fertilizer from the same supplier at USD 540 per metric ton, while Nepal purchased 900 metric tons, the fertilizer mentioned by the honorable questioner that India purchased at USD 540 per metric ton may be urea fertilizer, not DAP. The Agricultural Inputs Company accepted a bid from a company named Aditya Birla at USD 975 per metric ton, which is 0.46 percent less than the estimated cost of USD 905.56 per metric ton for urea fertilizer on May 15, 2026. Information has been received that on April 15, 2006, the neighboring friendly country India accepted bids from suppliers including Aditya Birla for the purchase of 2.4 million metric tons of urea fertilizer, including 1.4 million metric tons at USD 935 per metric ton and 1 million metric tons at USD 959 per metric ton. Therefore, based on this fact, it does not appear that the company purchased urea fertilizer from India at USD 540 per metric ton at the right time. Regarding why there is such a large difference between Nepal's and India's purchase prices, the facts mentioned above do not show a significant difference between Nepal's and India's fertilizer purchase prices. Furthermore, the rate at which the Government of India purchases is the price at which it arrives at any port in India from a third country, while in Nepal, additional costs such as transportation costs to unload the fertilizer from the ship, bagging, and delivery to the distributor's warehouse by rail or truck, and advance income tax are added to that amount. Therefore, the price at which India purchases incurs an additional cost of USD 120 to USD 150 per metric ton. Was fair competition ensured in fertilizer procurement? The fertilizer procurement process by the Government of Nepal through fertilizer distribution companies is carried out in accordance with the existing Public Procurement Act, 2063, and Regulations, 2064, and other prevailing economic laws and regulations. For this, the Public Procurement Monitoring Office under the Government of Nepal invites international bids through the e-GP system, and fertilizer suppliers can submit bids from anywhere in the world.

Because fertilizer is purchased, it is based on fair competition. In the past, 6-7 fertilizer supply companies used to participate in tenders, but due to Nepal's relatively small fertilizer market and multiple handling and logistic problems, currently 3 to 4 suppliers participate in the tender process. Therefore, I would like to inform the esteemed assembly that fertilizer is purchased in accordance with the existing procurement laws and regulations through competitive bidding. Regarding the question of whether an investigation should be conducted given the price difference of about double, as I have already stated, the fact is that the government has not purchased fertilizer at a price difference of double compared to India, and the contract has been made for purchasing fertilizer at a slightly lower price than India. Therefore, I would like to request that the facts and data are not as the honorable members have stated. If there is any collusion, corruption, or environment of malpractice in the purchase, I assure you that the government will act impartially to investigate and take action and maintain good governance. On one hand, there is a severe shortage of fertilizer across the country, and on the other hand, fertilizer is being purchased at a high price, which means a limited amount of fertilizer will arrive. Regarding this, the price of chemical fertilizer fluctuates daily in the international market, which directly affects Nepal, so the rate of every contract will vary. From the budget allocated for the purchase of chemical fertilizer, fertilizer distribution companies purchase chemical fertilizer by preparing an annual procurement plan according to the annual supply plan approved by the ministry, and in contracts where the purchase price is high, more subsidy is spent, and less fertilizer arrives. Recently, as the price of urea has decreased in the international market, the Agricultural Materials Company has accepted a tender for the purchase of 30,000 metric tons of urea fertilizer at USD 449.75 per metric ton on Asar 10th. However, the government cannot shirk its responsibility by saying that the price of fertilizer is high in the international market and therefore not purchasing it. This year, the government has supplied and distributed the highest amount of fertilizer to date. I would like to assure this assembly that efforts are being made to bring even more fertilizer in the new fiscal year 2083/084 than this year. Furthermore, regarding the budget of the Ministry of Agriculture, Forests and Environment for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084, I hope that the suggestions provided by the honorable members will be helpful in the implementation of the ministry's budget and programs for the upcoming fiscal year, and I express my sincere gratitude to you all again. Thank you. Honorable Minister of Foreign Affairs Mr. Shishir Khanal:- Honorable Chairperson, honorable members, the Government of Nepal is prioritizing work towards achieving good governance and economic prosperity by adhering to the Constitution of Nepal, foreign policy, and established principles of international relations. I have already informed this honorable house about the work of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on May 28, 2083, and June 17, 2083. Now, I am present to provide a brief overview to this honorable house, focusing on the annual policy and program and the proposed budget of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084. First of all, I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the honorable members for their thoughts and suggestions regarding the areas related to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Honorable members are already aware of the fundamental principles and constitutional guidance of Nepal's foreign policy. The annual policy and program for the upcoming fiscal year also continue this. Maintaining Nepal's sovereignty, territorial integrity, and national interests at the center, a balanced diplomacy based on the principles of the UN Charter, non-alignment, and peaceful coexistence will be adopted. Relations with neighboring and friendly countries will be expanded based on mutual benefit, respect, and multilateral cooperation. It also brings some new dimensions. The "Brand Nepal" campaign will be launched to expand soft power by establishing Nepal's unique identity, language, art, and heritage in the world, and to promote Nepali goods, services, culture, and tourism globally through diplomatic missions abroad. Regarding the budget for fiscal year 2083/084, the annual program and budget for the upcoming fiscal year 2083/084 have been determined for the effective implementation of the foreign policy directed by the constitution. The total proposed budget for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and its subordinate agencies for fiscal year 2083/084 is 8 billion 730 million rupees. This budget is 0.41 percent of the total budget and an increase of approximately 11 percent from the 7 billion 840 million allocated last year. Of this, approximately 7 billion 180 million (82 percent) is for current expenditure and 1 billion 550 million (approximately 18 percent) is for capital expenditure. The main goal is to transform traditional diplomacy into economic diplomacy. Under this, the aim is to attract foreign investment in areas such as information technology and innovation, education and health services, tourism infrastructure, energy, and information technology, making Nepal an international destination. A budget has been allocated to Nepali missions for economic diplomacy-related programs. 166.2 million rupees have been allocated for the operation of economic and cultural diplomacy programs by Nepali missions abroad. Since assuming leadership of the ministry, I have prioritized the digitalization of passport and consular services provided by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Nepali missions abroad, and this will continue in the upcoming fiscal year. A Diaspora Knowledge Bank and Knowledge Bank will be established to connect the capital, skills, experience, and technology of Nepalis living abroad with national development. For this, discussions have also begun with NRN friends to amend the NRN Act in a timely manner. Similarly, programs to further promote Nepal's soft power, including International Wellness Day, the birthplace of Buddha, the highest peak Sagarmatha, the Himalayan range, yoga and meditation, cultural diversity, the image of a peace-loving nation, and participation in international peace missions, have been planned. The Lumbini Fellowship program has been launched for young diplomats from SAARC countries. Similarly, the "International Dialogue Series" program will be initiated to discuss issues of international relations. The "Sagarmatha Dialogue" program is also planned to be organized in the upcoming fiscal year. The goal is to conduct mobile camps for passport services for Nepalis living abroad, strengthen the interoperability between the passport system and other related systems, and complete the necessary tasks to make the passport distribution process easier and faster within the stipulated time. For the first time, a budget has been allocated for the rescue of Nepali citizens in distress or stranded abroad. This is expected to address the main problem of rescuing Nepali citizens. Programs related to labor safety and awareness will be conducted through missions. To reduce the expenditure incurred in renting houses for Nepali missions abroad, the construction of buildings for the Nepali embassies in New Delhi, Bangkok, Canberra, and Riyadh will be expedited. A budget has also been allocated for this. Coordination is underway for improvements in the necessary legal and policy procedures related to public procurement. In addition to these, regarding some contemporary issues raised by the honorable members related to the ministry, I would like to briefly clarify those issues as well. Regarding the border issue, I have already informed the house on May 28, 2083, about the border issue raised by Honorable Renu Chand and other honorable members. The honorable members are also aware that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has already published a detailed description of Nepal's international borders. I would like to reiterate that we are always committed to resolving this issue through diplomatic dialogue based on historical treaties, agreements, and maps, in line with the spirit and sentiment of the close relationship between Nepal and India. Honorable Urmila Aryal and Honorable Savitri Malla had raised the issue of Nepali tea exports. I would like to inform you again that the government is continuously making efforts to resolve the problem seen in the export of Nepali tea to India, and this problem has now been resolved. Similarly, the issue raised by Honorable Rajendra Lakshmi Gaire and Honorable Ram Kumari Jhankri regarding opening Nepal-China border crossings and upgrading them to facilitate more convenient movement is a priority for the government. Honorable Samjhana Devkota had also raised this issue earlier. I had also informed this honorable house about this issue on June 17, 2083. Currently, three international border crossings between Nepal and the People's Republic of China, namely Hilsa-Pulha, Rasuwagadhi-Kerung, and Kodari-Jajarkot, as well as three bilateral crossings such as Lichi-Nichud, Korala-Mustang, Kimathanka-Chentang, and Olangchungola, and other traditional crossings are operational. This matter is also facilitated through coordination between the local administrations of Nepal and China. It is requested that efforts will be made to open bilateral agreement crossings or determine the modality of operation as needed by discussing and consulting with the Chinese side at the appropriate level and mechanism. Honorable Chandra Bahadur KC raised the issue of the Russia-Ukraine war and Nepalis. The Government of Nepal's policy is not to allow Nepali citizens to enlist in any foreign army except in countries with which traditional agreements have been concluded. Although it is not the policy of the Government of Nepal to allow Nepali citizens to enlist in any foreign army except in countries with which traditional agreements have been concluded, based on information provided by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) and the families of the victims, 9 Nepali citizens are currently in captivity in Ukraine. Similarly, among the Nepalis recruited into the Russian army, information has been received that 95 Nepali citizens are missing and 131 Nepalis have tragically died. A request has been made to the Russian government through the Nepali Embassy in Moscow for details of injured Nepalis, and the Government of Nepal has also requested the Russian government not to recruit Nepali citizens into the Russian army, including compensation for the missing and deceased Nepalis. I clearly raised this issue in a formal meeting with the Russian Ambassador a few days ago. Similarly, bringing back the bodies of Nepalis who have tragically died abroad is a matter of concern for all of us. We are serious about the issue of bringing back the bodies of Nepalis who have tragically died in Japan and other foreign countries, as raised by Honorable Roshri Meche. For those who went abroad for foreign employment with a labor permit or reached abroad by September 30, 2024, and received legalized labor permits from Nepali missions abroad, if they require rescue or assistance for any reason, or if their bodies need to be repatriated to Nepal, the concerned employer company can be compelled to do so.
